authority: Official consolidated Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 + official Gazette amendments/commencement + DCA FAQ as supporting interpretation
purpose: Rule 6 declaration layer for the September 2026 MVP. This is the legal interpretation layer; implementation validators remain separate.

rules.current_requirement: Name/address of manufacturer; where manufacturer is not packer, manufacturer and packer; imported package importer name/address. Rule 6 explanations assign responsibility in specified naming/brand-owner cases.
special_pathways: Food packages: this clause does not apply; Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and rules apply.

Electronic products: manufacturer/packer/importer name must be declared on the package itself; package must direct consumers to scan QR for address/related information when that information is provided through QR and not on package.

rules.current_requirement: Imported products must state country of origin/manufacture/assembly.
Common or generic name of commodity; packages containing more than one product require name and number or quantity of each product.
special_pathways: Electronic products: where this information is provided through QR and not on the package, the package must inform consumers to scan the QR code.

rules.current_requirement: Net quantity in standard unit of weight/measure, or number where packed/sold by number, subject to the applicable commodity and unit rules.
special_pathways: Electronic products: where quantity/size information covered by the 2023 QR amendment is provided through QR and not on the package, required QR instruction must be present.

rules.current_requirement: Use the current September 2026 manufacture month/year pathway; do not retain the older default wording that included 'or pre-packed or imported'. Apply the clause's explicit exceptions and other-law pathways.
exceptions: Other explicit commodity/other-law pathways must be routed conditionally.

rules.current_requirement: Where a commodity may become unfit for human consumption after a period, declare best-before/use-by month and year where applicable; where another law provides the relevant requirement, route to that law.
Declare retail sale price/maximum retail price in the prescribed form, subject to explicit exceptions.
exceptions: Domestic LPG cylinders whose price is covered under the Government Administrative Price Mechanism.

rules.current_requirement: MRP must clearly indicate the maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes and be expressed in Indian currency.
Where applicable, declare dimensions of the commodity and, where the different pieces have different dimensions, the dimensions of each different piece.
Capture other matters expressly specified elsewhere in the Rules as applicable to the commodity/package; do not treat this catch-all as a universal declaration.
Packages containing genetically modified food must bear 'GM' at the top of the principal display panel, subject to the applicable current food-law framework.
Packages containing soaps, shampoos, toothpastes and other cosmetics/toiletries must carry the prescribed vegetarian/non-vegetarian dot at the top of the principal display panel.
A label may be affixed on imported packages for making declarations required under the Rules, subject to the other applicable requirements.
Name, address, telephone number and e-mail address of the person/office that can be contacted for consumer complaints.
rules.interpretation: DCA FAQ confirms address may be referred to elsewhere on the label. For electronic products, telephone and e-mail remain package-level declarations while QR may provide related information when the amendment permits it.

rules.current_requirement: Individual stickers may not be used to alter or make declarations required under the Rules, except a sticker reducing MRP may be used if it does not cover the original MRP declaration. Stickers may be used for non-mandatory additional information under Rule 6(4).
rules.source_discrepancy: DCA FAQ labels the individual-sticker prohibition as Rule 6(2), while the consolidated rule text places it at Rule 6(3). Machine legal reference follows the consolidated text; FAQ remains supporting interpretation.

rules.current_requirement: Barcode/GTIN/QR code may be declared in addition to mandatory declarations; this is distinct from the 2023 electronic-product QR pathway, which modifies specific declaration instructions.
Applicable retail pre-packaged commodities require unit sale price on the principal display panel, subject to the rule's provisos/exemptions.
exceptions: Wholesale packages do not require unit sale price.
No declaration where MRP equals unit sale price.
Free additional quantity/value is excluded from the unit-sale-price computation as applicable.
DCA FAQ states unit sale price is not required on e-commerce websites.

rules.current_requirement: Unit sale price is inclusive of all taxes, displayed on PDP, and rounded to nearest two decimal places; whole-number values may be shown without decimals.

E-commerce entity must display Rule 6(1) mandatory declarations on the digital/electronic network except month/year manufacture or packing; marketplace responsibility follows the rule's intermediary conditions.
rules.special_note: DCA FAQ states unit sale price is not required on e-commerce websites.

rules.current_requirement: Every e-commerce entity selling imported products must provide a searchable and sortable product-listing filter specifying country of origin.
Replacement wording applies from 1 July 2027 and therefore is not the operative 6(10A) wording for September 2026 inspections.

For electronic products, where permitted information is declared through QR rather than on-package, the package must provide the prescribed instruction to scan the QR code; the package itself must still carry the declarations the amendment expressly requires on-package.

frozen_interpretation_notes: Rule 6(1)(g) is a routing/catch-all clause; commodity-specific declarations should be represented by separate rules rather than one universal validator.
Rule 6(7)-(9) are distinct sub-rules and should not be conflated with Rule 6(1)(g).
Rule 6(4A) permits additional barcode/GTIN/QR declarations; it does not by itself mean a QR code can replace every mandatory printed declaration.
G.S.R. 456(E) specifically modifies electronic-product declaration behavior and must be evaluated by product category and the exact affected declaration.
Unknown commodity category or unresolved other-law pathway must produce REVIEW, not PASS or FAIL.
This Rule 6 layer is frozen as a September 2026 working legal map; future amendments must create a new temporal version rather than mutate this baseline silently.
